SMTO-GWT-0067 — That clock speed isn't one this GPU supports

GUID: c9fe0942-fc04-53da-bfb4-de7f489d60a7
Slug: gpu-clock-value-unsupported
Domain: GWT · Subsystem: gpu

What happened

  • The lowest or highest speed you asked for isn't on this graphics card's list of supported speeds, or the lowest was set above the highest. Nothing was changed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. In the conversation, ask SMTO to show the clock capabilities for this GPU. It lists the exact speeds, in MHz, the card supports for its processor and its memory.
  2. Ask SMTO again to set the clock range, choosing both the lowest and the highest value from that list. SMTO only accepts exact supported speeds and never rounds to a nearby one.
  3. Make sure the lowest speed you give is not higher than the highest speed. A reversed range is always refused before any change is made.

What success looks like

  • SMTO reports that the card accepted the clock range you chose.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages the computer with the GPU. Don't guess speeds that aren't on the supported list.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The requested clock range is invalid: min_mhz exceeds max_mhz, or an endpoint is not among the device's reported supported clock values.

What this means

  • Clock validation found minimum greater than maximum or endpoints outside the device's reported supported values. The retained phase, target and receipt determine what executed. Rendering this definition adds no probe, retries, dispatch or changes to resource ownership.

Why this can happen

  • Clock validation found minimum greater than maximum or endpoints outside the device's reported supported values.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare each endpoint and their order with gpu.clock_capabilities for the same device.

How to fix it

  • Read gpu.clock_capabilities and choose min_mhz and max_mhz from clocks.supported_pairs (gpu_mhz values for set_gpu_clock_range, memory_mhz values for set_memory_clock_range), with min_mhz <= max_mhz. Endpoints are matched exactly and never clamped.
  • Choose endpoints reported by gpu.clock_capabilities with minimum no greater than maximum.

Retry and execution caution

  • Choose endpoints reported by gpu.clock_capabilities with minimum no greater than maximum.

How to verify the fix

  • Both explicitly chosen endpoints are supported and ordered; provider acknowledgment is retained without treating instantaneous frequency as proof of a lock.

What not to do

  • Do not replay uncertain mutations, kill GPU clients automatically or invent sensor values.

Technical notes

  • The retained phase, target and receipt determine what executed. Rendering this definition adds no probe, retries, dispatch or changes to resource ownership.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
